_comment: #3288 shrink-only ratchet for scripts/check-rls-route-coverage.mjs rule 2: per-file count of identity/credential-table statements that run on the bare pool with no RLS context, known, reviewed and NOT yet fixed. Lower a number when the route takes its read through a context helper (withAuthLookupContext / withAuthResolutionContext / withOAuthClientLookupContext / withTenantContext); raising it is a regression. Deleting this file sets every allowance to 0. Every entry needs a reason in _reasons (BASELINE_UNREASONED).

_reasons.app/api/cron/contract-renewal-check/rout: #3315. The recipient read (`users` joined to a tenant's active members) answers zero rows for every workspace, so the cron reports `checked/endingSoon` and mails nobody. Not folded into #3288 because the fix is a per-tenant decision, not a lookup privilege: this route holds a list of `tenantId`s and has to open one context per workspace (`withTenantContext(tid, tx => …)`), which is a design change to the cron rather than a wrapper around one statement.
_reasons.app/api/cron/sla-check/route.ts|PREAUTH_: #3315. The level-2+ escalation lookup reads the assigned user's email on the pool, gets nothing, and skips the send behind `if (user?.email)` — the breach is recorded and the rep is never told. Same class, same per-tenant answer, filed with the other two cron sites so one PR decides how cron establishes context at all (see also #3298, which is these routes' authentication gap rather than their RLS gap).
_reasons.app/api/cron/subscription-renewal-check/: #3315. The twin of contract-renewal-check's read, one workspace at a time, with the same zero-row answer and the same success-shaped log line.
